utterances.text: I see. But you must generally have known what had happened in Gllogjan and Irzniq on the 24th of March from general knowledge, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: When Otovic was killed was -- is this what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On that day you must have known, Mr. Stijovic, what happened, broadly speaking, in Gllogjan and Irzniq. There was a major all-day fire-fight, and you knew that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I need to interject if I may for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That I didn't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This witness is being asked to speculate about events he has no first-hand knowledge of. He's already told us that, in his own mind, the reason he were attacked was because they were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but nevertheless the line of questioning by Mr. Emmerson is admissible. Unfortunately, Mr. Emmerson, when the witness asked: "When Otovic was killed, was -- is that what you mean?" If you would have said "Yes," you might have perhaps received another answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's -- it's rather a selective description of what took place on the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, Witness, Mr. Stijovic, when you said: "When Otovic was killed, is this what you mean?" Do you know anything about the context in which Mr. Otovic was killed, what happened when he was killed? Do you -- did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I read in the media that Otovic had been killed, and Dragoslav and Mijat told me later that they had left their home that night, on that date, because of safety reasons. So this is all I know about this incident involving Otovic and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did the media not say anything about circumstances under which the death of Mr. Otovic occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if I would say -- would the media -- may the media have said that it was during an exchange of fire, something of the kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They said in the media that regular police patrol had come under attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you do remember some of the circumstances that were mentioned in the media, because earlier you said: I didn't know anything about it I don't know -- to quote you literally, Mr. Stijovic, you said: "Well, I read in the media that Otovic had been killed, and Dragoslav and Mijat told me later that they had left their home that night." And then I asked you: "Did the media not say anything about circumstances under which the death of Mr. Otovic occurred." And then you said: "I can't remember." And as an answer to my next question, you did remember that the media reported that Mr. Otovic was killed, as you said, during a -- that "when a regular police patrol had come under attack." So you learned something from the media about the circumstances. Would you please -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the media, in the media, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you be very precise, if asked questions, to fully explore your memory and see whether -- whether from the media or from any other source, whether you have any knowledge, whether you gained any knowledge, hearsay or direct knowledge, on the events. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm particularly interested in the fact that you've given evidence to this Tribunal that you knew of no reason why the villagers in Gllogjan might have wanted to hurt Mijat Stojanovic. You've given evidence before the Tribunal you knew of no reason, and the only reason that you could think of was the fact that you were Serbs, and that's what I'm trying to explore with you. Now, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson -- I'm sorry, Your Honour, I have to cut-in again. Mr. Emmerson keeps referring to a village -- the villagers attacking the Stojanovics. We have clear testimony for the record that it was the KLA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Perhaps that's causing some of the confusion that the witness is suffering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's -- Mr. Emmerson, be as precise as possible. Try to avoid summaries which might be criticised. Let's focus on the exact testimony of the witness, as I tried to do before. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've told us, Mr. Stijovic, that the people from Gllogjan who attacked you, both at the house and along the street, included people in civilian clothing, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Both in uniforms and in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly. There was civilian -- people in civilian clothes who attacked you; right?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Armed, armed civilians. Men, young men.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I fully understand that. People came out of their homes to attack you three, didn't they, along the way?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. They had surrounded the house probably before they did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As you were --

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Before we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As you were being taken into Gllogjan and to the house where you were beaten, people were coming out of their homes and attacking you, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: They were next to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, you had no idea what it was that those people might have against the Stojanovics?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that they had anything to do against them, that they had any reason to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Did you know that three teenagers had been killed in the attack on the 24th of March by the police?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were in Dashinoc on or about the 24th of March yourself?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You must have known, mustn't you, that the entire population of Gllogjan and Irzniq were displaced for several days immediately after this attack, that many of them came in the direction of your village, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This was no minor incident, Mr. Stijovic, and it occurred in the next village along from you. Are you really telling us you didn't know that?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't know about those teenagers getting killed, as you just put to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you --

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's not really a neighbouring village.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you not know about all of -- let me finish my question, please. Did you not know about all of the population of Gllogjan and Irzniq being displaced?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the first time that I hear about something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you not know that the Stojanovic family property had been used effectively as a military facility to launch the attack on the 24th of March by the police? Did you not know that?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, when you tell us the only possible reason could be that you were Serbs, had Dragoslav not told you that a few weeks earlier he'd been stopped by the KLA, treated appropriately, been questioned, and signed a piece of paper, and allowed home? Had he not told you that he had been treated perfectly appropriately when stopped by the KLA one night before the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Predrag or Dragan, as you call him, did you not know that he was, in fact, involved in the police operation on the 24th of March, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, because I was not in close contact with him. I mostly socialised with Dragoslav and I would -- half a year would pass by and then I would see Predrag again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to be absolutely clear, you've told us what you read in the newspaper about Otovic being murdered, as you call it. Your cousins asked you to come back to their house three weeks after the 24th of March without telling you of the scale of the conflict that had taken place there and in that village, did they?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think you mean yes, do you? They didn't tell you; is that what you're saying? They never mentioned anything of that kind to you?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they just mentioned that they had left their house that night when Otovic was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Did they tell you whether anyone had told them to leave their house?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us that this incident happened on a Saturday, perhaps we can help us date that. The 18th of April was a Friday in 1998 and the 19th of April was a Saturday. Are you sure it was a Saturday?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: One day before Easter, so it was a Saturday. I think it was a Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, it's my mistake. I've misread the calendar, you're quite right, the 18th of April is a Saturday. Do the teenagers in the villages -- do the teenagers in the villages go to school on Saturdays?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: On a Saturday? I don't know. I don't have this information at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You don't remember from when you were at school yourself? I mean, was it the practice to have school on Saturdays?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, sometimes you had school on Saturdays, sometimes you didn't; but in most cases you didn't go to school on Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, Mijat Stojanovic has given evidence to us today that a lot of the people he saw, including some people in uniform with weapons, were teenagers, some as young as 11 or 12. Does that accord with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, people of all ages were there. I think -- well, I can't be really sure, but I think they were aged 14 and upwards. Quite a lot of young people there, and they guarded us in the corridor with their rifles. They were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And none of them ever mentioned to you that it was their school friends who had been shot or their friends from the area who had been shot on the 24th of March by the police?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Stijovic, I'm essentially putting to you that what happened on the 18th of April isn't something that occurred because you three were Serbs; it's something which occurred because the village as a whole had been the subject of a terrible onslaught by the military police on the 24th of March and believed that the Stojanovic family were directly involved in that.

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, had the Stojanovic family been involved, then why would they inflict this kind of beating and torture on me when I had absolutely nothing to do with Glodjane and nothing to do with the Stojanovic family, and yet I shared their fate.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did your cousins tell you or did you read in the newspaper whether the police officer who was killed had been in a marked police vehicle or a civilian vehicle when he was killed?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Police officers did drive around in civilian vehicles, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, what Mr. Emmerson is trying to find out whether it ever came into your mind that the events, on the day where Mr. Otovic was killed, may have been the reason for what happened later in April. Did that ever cross your mind? Did you ever think about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I didn't really give it any thought. I didn't really think that this might have been the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, now you say you don't really think that this might have been the reason, at the same time you say: "I didn't really give it any thought." But if you conclude that this would not have been the reason, then you must have given it some thought, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't believe that this was the reason, what the Defence has just put to me, that we were beaten up because of the involvement in the attacks. Because why then would they beat me up the same as them when I was not even from the same village?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's your explanation. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson, I think. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very nearly finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mijat Stojanovic has given evidence that accusations of spying were made during the interrogations, spying for the Serb police. Do you remember those accusations being made?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Those accusations were not made to me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you hear them being made to the others; that is, Dragoslav and Mijat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I can't remember. I was certainly never accused of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Finally this: You mentioned Deli Lekaj, the man who passed by you with a weapon in his hand and warned you that a roadblock was being -- likely to be established in Pozar. Can I just be clear, he was trying to help you, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I understood him to mean, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He wasn't threatening you. He was trying to say: Look, if you want to avoid trouble for yourself, there's likely to be people setting up a roadblock.

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what his intention was, whether he said this for friendship, an account of our close friendship, or for whatever reason. At any rate, he said, If you ever get out of here alive, don't ever come back here. It's just a question of time how soon we get to Pozar and try not to let the same thing happen again, you coming here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And I think when you were interviewed about this by Mr. Di Fazio just a few days ago, you said that you took those words as advice rather than as a threat. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, I can't be expected to interpret his intentions, what exactly he meant. I did take it seriously, though, and I never tried to go back again to my own village.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you later hear that Deli Lekaj had been shot?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith, no questions I see. Mr. Harvey, no questions. Any need for further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Just two, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You were told by Mr. Lekaj, who you thought to be a member of the KLA, that you should not go back to your own home village because you could be hurt. Isn't that how you understood his statement?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't believe him to be a member of the Kosovo Liberation Army, but as soon as I saw him carrying a hand-held launcher, I knew that he was one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you were told by a member of the KLA that you should not go back to your own village because of why? Why did you think he was telling you not to go back to your own village?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: There are countless possible interpretations, but what I believed at the time is that his intentions were good, friendly. He saw the condition that I was in, and we had socialised in the past. He realised how poorly we had fared previously. I think he was well-intentioned. Maybe he wasn't, but I believed him to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm not quarrelling with that, sir. I'm just asking you: Did you believe -- what did you believe would happen if you had tried after that warning to go back to your village of Dasinovac?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I would have been arrested like Radosevic was later on. He probably knew that such things would happen. It was only a matter of time. Serbs who went that way later, to Dasinovac and that area, were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You were asked at great length about the possible motivation of the people who attacked the Stojanovic home, and I want to ask you, sir, is part of your earlier answer that you believed the attack was based on you being Serbs. Is part of that belief based on what they told you; namely: "Kosovo belonged to the Albanians"?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. What business have you? Yes, yes. And then it all tied-in. They were shouting that sort of thing: Kosovo belongs to us, it belongs to Albanians, and they cursed our Serb mothers, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And your belief that the attack on the -- on you and your cousins was based on your ethnicity, was that -- also -- was that belief also based in part on the other attacks you had seen on Serbs, both in your villages -- your village and the surrounding village?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the witness having said that he'd seen any attacks on Serbs at any point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm aware that he didn't say that, but of course you asked him -- not seen, but -- Mr. Kearney, perhaps you clarify whether he had seen or whether he is referring to the events he described before in which you sought to verify whether you were thinking about the same, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I would be happy to, Your Honour. Thank you for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your belief -- was your belief that the attack on you and your cousins was based in part or based because -- on the fact that you were Serbs on your viewing of the Malesa Culafic house and the reports in the media of attacks you had heard on Serbs and Serb homes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- perhaps we come at a point. I'll ask you quite simply. When you said it was because you were Serbs, you could not think about anything else, did you have in mind at that moment events you learned about and the type of events you spoke about earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it all ties in somehow, but my principal impression was that all of this happened because we were Serbs. Maybe what had happened when Otovic was killed was part of it for them, in their minds. But I personally had nothing whatsoever to do with the police or anything else in that particular area. I was from a different village altogether, yet I met the same sort of fate as the others did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although I joined the parties in my last question in calling for speculation, I certainly would discourage to continue with that. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Hoepfel has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, please. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I have the following clarifying question. You said you later left the country or you left Kosova. In which month of which year did you leave the region?

utterances.speaker: VESELIN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: May or June 1999. I'm not certain, May or June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: 1999. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, since I've got no further questions for you, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague. You've answered the questions by the parties and by the Bench. I wish you a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, would you please escort Mr. Stijovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, for calling me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to use the remaining couple of minutes first of all to deliver an oral decision, that is the Trial Chamber's decision on advance notification of witnesses. On the 19th of March, 2007, the Defence of Ramush Haradinaj addressed the Trial Chamber with a detailed proposal for advance notification of witnesses on a weekly basis. On the 23rd of March, the Prosecution responded to the proposal and rejected certain aspects of it as impractical. The Trial Chamber has considered the two proposals and adopts the Prosecution's counter-proposal as the way to proceed for the continuation of the Prosecution's case, at least in the short term. The Chamber expects the Prosecution to improve the organisation of its case presentation and strive to provide increasingly better notice to both the Defence and the Trial Chamber. Thus, the proposal we are adopting, at least for the short term, involves providing proofing notes to the Defence no later than 27 hours in advance, and proofing notes and witness statements to the Trial Chamber no later than 24 hours in advance of the testimony. Furthermore, it includes providing the Defence and the Trial Chamber each Thursday with a list of witnesses for the week to come. This list should include the estimation of time for examination-in-chief, if this differs from what has been mentioned in the 65 ter summary. The Prosecution should also - as it has been done so far - provide to Defence and the Trial Chamber with a list of exhibits to be used for each witness. Finally, the Prosecution has agreed to provide the Defence seven days' notice on when to call certain witnesses. These witnesses are specified in an annex to the Haradinaj Defence's proposal and in a mail, an e-mail, to the Prosecution from the Defence of Lahi Brahimaj on the 20th of March, 2007. This concludes the decision on advance notification of witnesses. We will adjourn unless there's any procedural issue to be urgently raised. We'll then adjourn -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there's one matter I ought to raise. Your Honour will very shortly be receiving within the next hour and a half the finalised submissions on proofing. Partly for reasons of time and partly for other reasons that essentially involve the way in which work has been managed, I regret to say there will be two documents rather than one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll see that and -- so we expect to receive them today, both the documents. Then we adjourn until Monday, the 2nd of April, quarter past 2.00 in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
